quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #14
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What should you do if the road ahead is flooded?

options.text: Slam on the brakes.
Do not drive through it. Turn around and find another route.
Drive only in the center of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive through it. Turn around and find another route.
questions.explanation: Never drive on a flooded road. Water may hide dangers like deep holes or debris. If you see a flooded area, turn around and find a different way to your destination.

questions.question: What do drivers need to do on interstate highways?

options.text: Be able to drive safely at high speeds.
Stay alert at all times.
Both of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both of the above.
questions.explanation: Safe interstate driving requires you to stay alert and drive safely at high speeds.

questions.question: What often happens when you brake hard on ice and snow?

options.text: You stop faster.
Your front wheels lock up and you lose steering control.
Your brakes stay from freezing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your front wheels lock up and you lose steering control.
questions.explanation: Hard braking on snow and ice can lock your front wheels. This makes you lose control of steering. Drive slowly on these surfaces to avoid needing hard braking.

questions.question: Why is extra space in front of a large truck important?

options.text: So other drivers can merge onto the freeway.
So the truck driver has room to stop.
So other drivers can slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: So the truck driver has room to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks are heavier and take longer to stop than cars traveling at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down or stop.

questions.question: If dust or smoke blocks your view of other vehicles, you should slow down and turn on your:

options.text: Emergency flashers.
Parking lights.
Headlights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Headlights.
questions.explanation: Turn on your headlights whenever you cannot see other vehicles clearly. This helps other drivers see you too.

questions.question: To check your blind spot when changing lanes, you should look:

options.text: Only in your left side mirror.
Over your left or right shoulder.
Only in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over your left or right shoulder.
questions.explanation: Your mirrors cannot show all areas around your car. These hidden areas are called blind spots. Look over your shoulder to check for vehicles before changing lanes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A railroad crossing is ahead. Get ready to stop.
You will always stop at the railroad crossing ahead.
Stop and wait for a signal before crossing the railroad tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: A railroad crossing is ahead. Get ready to stop.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming. Look and listen, slow down, and be ready to stop. Wait for trains to pass before continuing.

questions.question: What is the correct order of traffic light colors from top to bottom?

options.text: Red, yellow, green.
Red, green, yellow.
Green, red, yellow.

questions.correctAnswerText: Red, yellow, green.
questions.explanation: Traffic lights are always arranged from top to bottom: red, yellow, and green. Red means stop, yellow means caution, and green means go.

questions.question: Before you enter a curve, you should:

options.text: Use your turn signal.
Slow down.
Brake hard.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: You can drive slower than the speed limit when conditions require it, but never faster. Curves require reduced speed for safety. Other situations needing slower speeds include hills with limited sight, slippery roads, and areas with pedestrians or animals.

questions.question: How do you make a proper right turn?

options.text: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the centerline before turning.
Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
Approach from the right lane, but move toward the middle of the street before turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, slow down, and move to the lane closest to the right curb before turning.
questions.explanation: Before turning right, use your turn signal to warn other drivers. Slow down and approach from the right lane, staying as close as possible to the right curb.

questions.question: Why is it more dangerous to drive at night than during the day?

options.text: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
The road is always more slippery at night.
Your reaction time is slower at night.

questions.correctAnswerText: You cannot see as far ahead at night.
questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as far ahead because of low light and glare from oncoming headlights. Always use your headlights and drive with extra caution in the dark.

questions.question: What must you do when you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway?

options.text: Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.
Change lanes and maintain your current speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.
questions.explanation: Construction signs warn you about workers, slow-moving equipment, and closed lanes ahead. Reduce your speed and be ready to slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line mean?

options.text: Vehicles driving in both directions may pass.
Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line on your side means you can pass other vehicles.

questions.question: What does a pentagon-shaped sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign.
Regulatory sign.
School zone or school crossing sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: School zone or school crossing sign.
questions.explanation: A five-sided sign warns drivers about school zones. It alerts you that children or pedestrians may be crossing the road.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?

options.text: Upcoming intersections.
Road construction.
Road curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to immediate dangers ahead. This sign warns you about an upcoming curve to the right.

questions.question: What does this sign tell you?

options.text: No turns are allowed on the road.
The road narrows ahead.
There is a series of curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a series of curves ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to immediate dangers ahead. This sign warns about a winding road with multiple curves.

questions.question: What are "No zones" around trucks?

options.text: Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop or maneuver safely.
Areas behind the truck where cars have enough space to travel safely.
Areas where cars have several car lengths between them and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or are too close for the truck driver to stop or maneuver safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are areas around trucks where cars cannot be seen or are so close that the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely. Being in a "No zone" greatly increases crash risk.

questions.question: What does this sign warn you about?

options.text: The right lane is ending and traffic should merge left.
The road curves ahead.
There are upcoming intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending and traffic should merge left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert you to immediate dangers ahead. This sign warns that a lane is ending and you need to merge left.

questions.question: What must you do at an intersection with a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Wait for the green light before proceeding.
Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.
Stop before crossing the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and be alert. Watch for crossing traffic and pedestrians before you proceed.

questions.question: What should you know about driving on gravel or dirt roads?

options.text: Your tires grip the road better than on pavement.
Your tires have less traction than on pavement, so you must slow down.
Visibility is better than on pavement.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your tires have less traction than on pavement, so you must slow down.
questions.explanation: Gravel and dirt roads have less traction than paved roads. You must slow down, as stopping takes longer and skidding is more likely when turning.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: You can pass from the lane with the solid yellow line.
No one can pass from either direction.
You can pass from the lane with the broken yellow line.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can pass from the lane with the broken yellow line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means you can cross it to pass. A solid yellow line means you cannot cross it to pass. When they are together, only the lane with the broken line can pass.

questions.question: You are on a one-way street. When can you turn left onto another one-way street?

options.text: When you speed up before the turn.
When traffic moves to the right.
When traffic moves to the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: When traffic moves to the left.
questions.explanation: You can turn left onto a one-way street only if traffic on that street moves to the left. You cannot turn left onto a one-way street where traffic moves to the right.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles are not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They alert drivers to watch for people or vehicles that may cross the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Do not enter.
Yield the right-of-way.
Reserved parking for people with disabilities.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter.
questions.explanation: This sign is posted where you cannot enter, such as on one-way streets or wrong-way expressway ramps.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What should you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the car.
questions.explanation: You must leave a note with your name, phone number, and address on any vehicle or property you hit.

questions.question: Remove all snow, frost, and ice from:

options.text: Just the windshield.
All windows.
Just the windshield and passenger window.

questions.correctAnswerText: All windows.
questions.explanation: You must be able to see clearly from all windows and mirrors. Remove all snow, ice, and frost before you drive.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road is changing direction or getting narrower.
No right turn.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road is changing direction or getting narrower.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead will change direction or become narrower. You may see this sign on sharp curves or before narrow bridges.

questions.question: How do alcohol and drugs affect driving skills?

options.text: They reduce alertness.
They reduce coordination.
They reduce both alertness and coordination.

questions.correctAnswerText: They reduce both alertness and coordination.
questions.explanation: Alcohol and drugs harm many skills needed for safe driving, including reaction time, coordination, alertness, and concentration.

questions.question: How do stopping distance and crash severity change with vehicle speed?

options.text: They decrease as speed increases.
They are not affected by speed.
They increase as speed increases.

questions.correctAnswerText: They increase as speed increases.
questions.explanation: Higher speeds cause longer stopping distances and more severe crashes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a downgrade or hill ahead.
Road construction area.
The road ahead is getting narrower.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a downgrade or hill ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a steep or long downgrade or hill ahead that may have sharp curves.
